title: Vijay Mallya flees India after Kingfisher collapse
trigger: Vijay Mallya, chairman of Kingfisher Airlines, fled India in March 2016 after the airline collapsed under mounting debt and allegations of loan default and fund diversion.

timeline.event: Kingfisher Airlines ceases operations after accumulating massive debt
Indian banks file case against Mallya for defaulting on Rs 90 billion in loans
Mallya leaves India for London as banks seek to recover dues
Indian government declares Mallya a fugitive economic offender
UK court approves Mallya's extradition to India

outcome.summary: Vijay Mallya fled India in March 2016 after Kingfisher Airlines collapsed with approximately Rs 90 billion in unpaid loans. He was declared a fugitive economic offender in 2017. UK courts approved his extradition to India in 2019, but he remains in London fighting extradition. Indian banks continue to pursue recovery through civil and criminal proceedings.

claims.text: Kingfisher Airlines ceased operations on October 1, 2012 after accumulating massive debt
Indian banks filed a case against Vijay Mallya on February 29, 2016 for defaulting on Rs 90 billion in loans
Vijay Mallya left India for London on March 2, 2016 as banks sought to recover dues
The Indian government declared Mallya a fugitive economic offender on April 18, 2017
A UK court approved Mallya's extradition to India on December 10, 2019
